text: LoRA freezes a pretrained network and injects small trainable low-rank matrices into attention and MLP layers. This cuts memory and makes multi-adapter serving practical.
QLoRA stores base weights in 4-bit precision and keeps adapters in higher precision. On a 4GB GPU it is often the only way to fine-tune a 1B-class instruct model.
Continued pre-training adapts a base LM to a domain corpus before instruction tuning. Keep documents reasonably long and avoid mixing chat templates into raw text.
Full-parameter fine-tuning updates every weight. It needs more VRAM than LoRA, so teams usually reserve it for tiny models or large multi-GPU boxes.
Tokenizers split text into subword units. Sequence length limits how many tokens fit in one training example; longer contexts raise memory roughly linearly.
Gradient accumulation simulates a larger batch without increasing peak activation memory. Many Unsloth recipes use batch size 1 with accumulation of 4 or 8.
Evaluation prompts should look like real user requests. Store a reference answer when you want automatic similarity or exact-match scoring after training.
MinIO stores dataset blobs and job snapshots. The manager records object names; workers download them during audit and training.
RabbitMQ decouples upload from scoring and training. Dataset jobs and fine-tune jobs use separate queues so a long train does not block audits.
A healthy raw-text corpus for pretrain or CPT is just clean paragraphs. No chat roles, no preference labels—only the text field.
